notes:
CIRCUIT: a multi-stage bipolar chain. A resistive bias string runs +15V rail -> R#1 15k -> (+10V tap) -> R#4 15k -> tap n5 -> R#8 150ohm -> (+6V tap) -> R#9 15k -> (+5V node). Each tap feeds the emitter of a PNP whose collector drives an NPN standing on the bottom ground rail; a two-diode string (D#5, D#11) level-shifts from the base of NPN #3 down to the base of PNP #15. The arrows labelled +15V/+10V/+6V/+5V/+3V are node-voltage annotations (V-DC one-port symbols), each tacked onto the node it labels. 24 components, 16 nets.

NET MAP:
  n1  = +15V top rail (y~150): arrow #0 (569,112), top of R#1, collector of NPN #3 (824,249).
  n2  = +10V tap between R#1 and R#4 at (315,242): R#1 bottom, arrow #2, R#4 top.
  n5  = node at (306,413): R#4 bottom, left end of R#8 (150 ohm), emitter (top lead) of PNP #10.
  n7  = +6V tap at (494,417): right end of R#8, left end of R#9 (15k), arrow #6, emitter (top lead) of PNP #12.
  n4  = +5V node at (828,434) and the right column down to y~575: right end of R#9, emitter of NPN #3, arrow #7, emitter (top lead) of PNP #15, collector of NPN #19.
  n3  = short wire (705,300)-(785,297): base of NPN #3 and the top (anode) lead of D#5. Only 2 terminals - verified in the ink that nothing else joins it.
  n6  = the x~700 wire from D#5 bottom (703,364) to D#11 top (699,465), which hops over the 15k rail at (717,427). 2 terminals.
  n10 = x~700 column from D#11 bottom (698,511) down to (703,730): base of PNP #15 (via the branch at S25), collector of NPN #20.
  n14 = collector (bottom lead) of PNP #15 -> base of NPN #19.
  n9  = base of PNP #10 (271,475) <- emitter (top lead) of PNP #14.
  n8  = collector (bottom lead) of PNP #10 down the x~300 column to the collector of NPN #22 (298,752). 2 terminals.
  n13 = +3V node at (44,531): arrow #13, base of PNP #14, top of R#17 (50k).
  n11 = collector (bottom lead) of PNP #12 down the x~490 column to (490,719), then right along y~715 to the base of NPN #20; also the collector of NPN #21.
  n12 = base (right lead) of PNP #12 down the x~614 column to the top of R#18 (50k); the second +3V arrow #16 taps it at (617,597).
  n15 = the y~780 wire between the base of NPN #22 and the base of NPN #21. 2 terminals as drawn.
  0   = bottom ground rail y~850: emitters of NPN #19/#20/#21/#22, collector (bottom lead) of PNP #14 via the x~168 column, bottoms of R#17 and R#18, GND #23.

JUDGEMENT CALLS:
  S11 (717,427) -> CROSSING, overriding the tracer's default junction. At 12x the vertical wire leaves x=703 at y=411, arcs right to x=717 at the rail's height, and returns to x=703 at y=440: a textbook semicircular hop, with the 15k rail running dead straight through it. Encoded as explicit edge groups [[28,37],[35,36]] rather than 'crossing' because the two arc halves leave the site at ~135deg and ~225deg, which the opposite-branch rule cannot be trusted to pair. The junction reading would have merged D#5's cathode and D#11's anode into the +5V node n4, putting D#5 in parallel with the base-emitter junction of NPN #3 and shorting the middle of the diode string to the output node.
  S10 (494,417) -> JUNCTION, overriding the tracer's default crossing (its hop score of 7.1 is a false positive from the arrowhead above). inkmap shows a plain X: the vertical stroke is 3 px wide and straight through (x 493-495 above, 492-494 below), the crossing widens only to the 5-6 px two strokes must give, and there is no blob 3x the stroke in both axes and no jog. This drafter draws an unmistakable hop when he means 'not connected' (S11 and S34 on this same sheet), so a bare X is a junction. It also puts the emitter of PNP #12 on the tap the '+6V' arrow annotates, matching every other stage (emitter of #10 on the R#4/R#8 tap at S9, emitter of #15 on the +5V node at S12). The crossing reading would leave R#8 and R#9 as a pointless untapped 2-terminal series pair and would make the '+6V' label belong to the emitter alone.
  S34 (619,794) -> CROSSING, agreeing with the default (hop=27.9). Clear semicircular hop where the bottom lead of R#18 (heading down to the ground rail at S40) passes the y~790 wire carrying n11 to the base of NPN #20. A junction here would tie the base of #20 straight to the grounded end of R#18.
  S12 (828,434) -> JUNCTION. dot=2.5: a fat retraced blob where the emitter column of NPN #3, the 15k rail, the +5V arrow lead and the column down to #15/#19 all meet. Four-way node, no hop.
  S1 (566,148), S9 (306,413), S22 (44,531), S23 (826,533), S25 (705,619), S32 (490,719), S24 (614,597), S37 (830,837), S38 (699,844), S39 (174,848), S40 (606,849), S42 (475,854), S43 (299,857) -> JUNCTION. Every one is an unambiguous T (a wire ending on another wire), so no crossing reading exists; checked individually in the 5x crops.
  Non-critical sites S0/S2/S5/S6/S7/S15/S17/S18/S19/S26/S27/S29/S30/S31 are handwritten captions ('+15','+10V','+6V','+5V','150 ohm','+3V','50k') touching wire or symbol ink; left at default, none of them changes the netlist.

PORT / PIN-ORDER FIXES:
  All four BJT-PNP (#10, #12, #14, #15) had collector and emitter swapped by the tracer. In every one the arrowhead sits on the UPPER lead and points into the base bar, so the top lead is the emitter and the bottom lead the collector; remapped to the required (collector, base, emitter) order: #10 {t0=p2 bottom, t1=p0 left, t2=p1 top}, #12 {t0=p0 bottom, t1=p2 right, t2=p1 top}, #14 {t0=p0 bottom, t1=p1 left, t2=p2 top}, #15 {t0=p2 bottom, t1=p1 left, t2=p0 top}. The physical reading agrees: each PNP emitter sits on a bias-string tap (the higher potential) and each collector drives an NPN below it.
  #16 (+3V arrow): terminal 0 retargeted from p0 (632,625), which is a stroke of the handwritten '+3V' caption, to p2 (619,597) - the 3-px stub where the arrow's tail meets the x~614 column above R#18. Without this the arrow sat alone on a 1-terminal net (the tracer's own warning).
  All five BJT-NPN (#3, #19, #20, #21, #22) were re-checked at 5x: the arrowhead is on the lower lead pointing away from the base, so collector=top, base=side, emitter=bottom exactly as the tracer had them. #22 is mirrored (base lead to the right) but still emitter-down. R#9's third port candidate (564,446) is a stroke of the '15k' caption, not a lead; left unused.

CLASSES: no changes; every symbol matches its label (4 PNP with the emitter arrow into the base, 5 NPN with the arrow out of the base, 2 diodes drawn anode-up, 6 resistors, 6 one-port supply/annotation arrows, 1 GND).

UNRESOLVED / NOTED: n3 (base of #3 + anode of D#5) and n15 (the two tied bases of #21 and #22) each touch only two terminals and drive nothing else; I traced both wires at high zoom and nothing further attaches, so they are recorded as drawn even though they leave those branches without a bias path.
